audit_status.source_base: Greek 2 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for earthly tent/heavenly dwelling, walking by trust, judgment seat, love of Messiah, new creation, reconciliation, ambassadors.

verses.restored: For we know that if our earthly house of the tent is taken down, we have a building from the Divine, a house not made with hands, age-long in the heavens.

familiar.text: For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

modern.text: Now we know that if the earthly tent we live in is dismantled, we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands.

original.text: Οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι ἐὰν ἡ ἐπίγειος ἡμῶν οἰκία τοῦ σκήνους καταλυθῇ, οἰκοδομὴν ἐκ θεοῦ ἔχομεν οἰκίαν ἀχειροποίητον αἰώνιον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.

verses.restored: For in this we groan, longing to be clothed over with our dwelling from heaven,

familiar.text: For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven:

modern.text: For in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling,

original.text: καὶ γὰρ ἐν τούτῳ στενάζομεν, τὸ οἰκητήριον ἡμῶν τὸ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐπενδύσασθαι ἐπιποθοῦντες,

verses.restored: if indeed, having been clothed, we will not be found naked.

familiar.text: If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.

modern.text: because when we are clothed, we will not be found naked.

original.text: ⸂εἴ γε⸃ καὶ ⸀ἐνδυσάμενοι οὐ γυμνοὶ εὑρεθησόμεθα.

verses.restored: For while we are in the tent, we groan, being burdened, not because we wish to be unclothed, but clothed over, so that the mortal may be swallowed by life.

familiar.text: For we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.

modern.text: So while we are in this tent, we groan under our burdens, because we do not wish to be unclothed but clothed, so that our mortality may be swallowed up by life.

original.text: καὶ γὰρ οἱ ὄντες ἐν τῷ σκήνει στενάζομεν βαρούμενοι ἐφʼ ᾧ οὐ θέλομεν ἐκδύσασθαι ἀλλʼ ἐπενδύσασθαι, ἵνα καταποθῇ τὸ θνητὸν ὑπὸ τῆς ζωῆς.

verses.restored: The One who worked us into this very thing is the Divine, who gave us the pledge/down payment of the Spirit.

familiar.text: Now he that hath wrought us for the selfsame thing is God, who also hath given unto us the earnest of the Spirit.

modern.text: And God has prepared us for this very purpose and has given us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come.

original.text: ὁ δὲ κατεργασάμενος ἡμᾶς εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο θεός, ⸀ὁ δοὺς ἡμῖν τὸν ἀρραβῶνα τοῦ πνεύματος.

verses.restored: Therefore, always being courageous and knowing that while at home in the body we are away from home from the Lord,

familiar.text: Therefore we are always confident, knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord:

modern.text: Therefore we are always confident, although we know that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord.

original.text: Θαρροῦντες οὖν πάντοτε καὶ εἰδότες ὅτι ἐνδημοῦντες ἐν τῷ σώματι ἐκδημοῦμεν ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου,

verses.restored: for we walk through trust, not through sight.

familiar.text: (For we walk by faith, not by sight:)

modern.text: For we walk by faith, not by sight.

original.text: διὰ πίστεως γὰρ περιπατοῦμεν, οὐ διὰ εἴδους—

verses.restored: Yet we are courageous and think it beautiful/good rather to be away from home from the body and at home with the Lord.

familiar.text: We are confident, I say, and willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.

modern.text: We are confident, then, and would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord.

original.text: θαρροῦμεν δὲ καὶ εὐδοκοῦμεν μᾶλλον ἐκδημῆσαι ἐκ τοῦ σώματος καὶ ἐνδημῆσαι πρὸς τὸν κύριον·

verses.restored: Therefore also we make it our aim, whether at home or away, to be pleasing to him.

familiar.text: Wherefore we labour, that, whether present or absent, we may be accepted of him.

modern.text: So we aspire to please Him, whether we are here in this body or away from it.

original.text: διὸ καὶ φιλοτιμούμεθα, εἴτε ἐνδημοῦντες εἴτε ἐκδημοῦντες, εὐάρεστοι αὐτῷ εἶναι.

verses.restored: For we all must be manifested before the judgment seat of Messiah, so that each may receive the things through the body according to what one practiced, whether good or harmful.

familiar.text: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.

modern.text: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad. Ambassadors for Christ

original.text: τοὺς γὰρ πάντας ἡμᾶς φανερωθῆναι δεῖ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ βήματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἵνα κομίσηται ἕκαστος τὰ διὰ τοῦ σώματος πρὸς ἃ ἔπραξεν, εἴτε ἀγαθὸν εἴτε ⸀φαῦλον.

verses.restored: Knowing therefore the reverence/fear of the Lord, we persuade humans, and we have been made manifest to the Divine; and I hope also in your consciences we have been made manifest.

familiar.text: Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences.

modern.text: Therefore, since we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to persuade men. What we are is clear to God, and I hope it is clear to your conscience as well.

original.text: Εἰδότες οὖν τὸν φόβον τοῦ κυρίου ἀνθρώπους πείθομεν, θεῷ δὲ πεφανερώμεθα· ἐλπίζω δὲ καὶ ἐν ταῖς συνειδήσεσιν ὑμῶν πεφανερῶσθαι.

verses.restored: We are not again recommending ourselves to you, but giving you opportunity for boasting on our behalf, so that you may have an answer toward those boasting in face and not in heart.

familiar.text: For we commend not ourselves again unto you, but give you occasion to glory on our behalf, that ye may have somewhat to answer them which glory in appearance, and not in heart.

modern.text: We are not commending ourselves to you again. Instead, we are giving you an occasion to be proud of us, so that you can answer those who take pride in appearances rather than in the heart.

original.text: ⸀οὐ πάλιν ἑαυτοὺς συνιστάνομεν ὑμῖν, ἀλλὰ ἀφορμὴν διδόντες ὑμῖν καυχήματος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, ἵνα ἔχητε πρὸς τοὺς ἐν προσώπῳ καυχωμένους καὶ ⸂μὴ ἐν⸃ καρδίᾳ.

verses.restored: For if we were out of our mind, it was for the Divine; if sober-minded, it is for you.

familiar.text: For whether we be beside ourselves, it is to God: or whether we be sober, it is for your cause.

modern.text: If we are out of our mind, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.

original.text: εἴτε γὰρ ἐξέστημεν, θεῷ· εἴτε σωφρονοῦμεν, ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: For the love of Messiah holds us together, having judged this: that one died for all; therefore all died.

familiar.text: For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead:

modern.text: For Christ’s love compels us, because we are convinced that One died for all, therefore all died.

original.text: ἡ γὰρ ἀγάπη τοῦ Χριστοῦ συνέχει ἡμᾶς, κρίναντας τοῦτο ⸀ὅτι εἷς ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανεν· ἄρα οἱ πάντες ἀπέθανον·

verses.restored: And he died for all, so that those living may no longer live for themselves, but for the One who died for them and was raised.

familiar.text: And that he died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again.

modern.text: And He died for all, that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised again.

original.text: καὶ ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ἵνα οἱ ζῶντες μηκέτι ἑαυτοῖς ζῶσιν ἀλλὰ τῷ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἀποθανόντι καὶ ἐγερθέντι.

verses.restored: So then, from now on we know no one according to flesh. Even if we have known Messiah according to flesh, yet now we no longer know him so.

familiar.text: Wherefore henceforth know we no man after the flesh: yea, though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now henceforth know we him no more.

modern.text: So from now on we regard no one according to the flesh. Although we once regarded Christ in this way, we do so no longer.

original.text: Ὥστε ἡμεῖς ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν οὐδένα οἴδαμεν κατὰ σάρκα· ⸀εἰ καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν κατὰ σάρκα Χριστόν, ἀλλὰ νῦν οὐκέτι γινώσκομεν.

verses.restored: So if anyone is in Messiah: new creation. The old things passed away; look, new things have come to be.

familiar.text: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.

modern.text: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!

original.text: ὥστε εἴ τις ἐν Χριστῷ, καινὴ κτίσις· τὰ ἀρχαῖα παρῆλθεν, ἰδοὺ γέγονεν ⸀καινά·

verses.restored: But all things are from the Divine, who reconciled us to himself through Messiah and gave us the service/ministry of reconciliation,

familiar.text: And all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation;

modern.text: All this is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:

original.text: τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ καταλλάξαντος ἡμᾶς ἑαυτῷ ⸀διὰ Χριστοῦ καὶ δόντος ἡμῖν τὴν διακονίαν τῆς καταλλαγῆς,

verses.restored: namely, that the Divine was in Messiah reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses to them, and placing in us the word of reconciliation.

familiar.text: To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation.

modern.text: that God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, not counting men’s trespasses against them. And He has committed to us the message of reconciliation.

original.text: ὡς ὅτι θεὸς ἦν ἐν Χριστῷ κόσμον καταλλάσσων ἑαυτῷ, μὴ λογιζόμενος αὐτοῖς τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, καὶ θέμενος ἐν ἡμῖν τὸν λόγον τῆς καταλλαγῆς.

verses.restored: Therefore we are ambassadors on behalf of Messiah, as the Divine appealing through us. We ask on behalf of Messiah: be reconciled to the Divine.

familiar.text: Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ’s stead, be ye reconciled to God.

modern.text: Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ: Be reconciled to God.

original.text: ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ οὖν πρεσβεύομεν ὡς τοῦ θεοῦ παρακαλοῦντος διʼ ἡμῶν· δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ, καταλλάγητε τῷ θεῷ.

verses.restored: The One who knew no sin/misalignment he made sin/misalignment for us, so that in him we might become righteousness/justice of the Divine.

familiar.text: For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.

modern.text: God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.

original.text: ⸀τὸν μὴ γνόντα ἁμαρτίαν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίαν ἐποίησεν, ἵνα ἡμεῖς γενώμεθα δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ.

translation_notes: Tent/house/clothing imagery is embodied resurrection hope, not contempt for the body. The mortal is swallowed by life, not erased.
Reconciliation is central: God in Messiah reconciles the world and entrusts the community with the word and service of reconciliation.
